ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (as amended by Decree 2553 of 2010) creating the Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF); Law 1121 of 2006; Decree 1674 of 2016 (UBO obligations under the AML/CFT framework); Superintendency of Companies Resolution 100-000005 of 2022 and Circular External 005 of 2023 (SARO and UBO registration requirements); Regulatory Decree 1074 of 2015 (mercantile registry and entity formation).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chamber of Commerce of the shareholder's domicile / equivalent foreign registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; bilateral consular legalization only if the source state is not a Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granting incorporation authority to a Colombian resident attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Convention jurisdictions, Consular Legalization by the Colombian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner (identity pages, certified)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority / notary in source country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for passport certification, unless notarial certification is accepted by the Colombian registry in review

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Disclosure Form and AML/CFT declaration (Form for Report of Beneficial Ownership)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Superintendency of Companies (electronic filing through the SIRUBO portal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Digital filing with electronic signature; no apostille required for the internal form

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / solvency of the sole shareholder (if corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority or registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against the UIAF consolidated PEP list, Colombian Office of the Attorney General sanctions registry, UN Security Council consolidated list (UNSC Res. 1267/1988/2231), OFAC SDN List, and domestic terrorist organization lists under Law 1121 of 2006. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, family member, or close associate; internal risk rating must be documented prior to incorporation and filed with the compliance officer designated under Circular External 005 of 2023.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the local Chamber of Commerce virtual portal (e.g., Bogotá Chamber of Commerce 'CCB en Línea' for private limited company name requests)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be filed in Spanish or Spanish transliteration of foreign words; the Registry accepts Latin characters, but the legal standard requires that the name be pronounceable under Spanish phonetics and not be contrary to public order or morality. Foreign brand names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet ensuring no misleading similarity with existing registrations in Colombia.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must file, within 10 business days of the rejection notice, a formal reconsideration (recurso de reposición) with the same Chamber of Commerce through the RUES portal or in person, attaching arguments of non-confusion and, if applicable, a written authorization from the ministry or competent authority that issued the prior approval for the prohibited token. If the Chamber of Commerce maintains the rejection, the applicant may file a subsidiary appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendent of Companies, whose decision exhausts administrative remedies. A renewed name application under a distinct alternative name does not forfeit appeal rights but is processed simultaneously.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance is conditional: the S.A.S. may use a virtual office address for administrative registry purposes, but a physical registered address (domicilio social) must be identified as the place where management and internal corporate governance are located. For a resin statue crafting (ISIC 3240) garage-workshop storage model, a residential garage may serve as the domicilio if zoning laws do not prohibit light manufacturing; however, the Superintendency of Companies requires that the registered address be complete (street, number, city, municipality) and that the entity maintain operational substance. Virtual-only shared office is permissible for recordkeeping but is high risk for physical inspection because commercial substance requires at least minimal inventory storage or packing capability; for this low-risk craft business, a virtual office plus a domestic grinding and casting subcontractor is acceptable on documentary substance, but legal counsel should register the residential garage as the operational domicile.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008, Articles 1–54 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), in supplementation of Código de Comercio Decreto 410 de 1971, Articles 110, 354 and 373; governed procedurally by Ley 2069 de 2020 (Entrepreneurship Law) for digital expedited formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed) executed by all shareholders, or Escritura Pública (public deed) granted before a Notary Public when in-kind contributions are made or at shareholders' election; the instrument must be filed for registration in the Mercantile Registry and RUES.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum or maximum capital; the bylaws set subscribed capital which may be zero or nominal. Per Article 5 of Ley 1258 de 2008, the bylaws determine payment installments provided the entire subscribed capital is paid within two years from subscription; no escrow account is required, and in-kind contributions must be described and valued in accordance with Article 128 of the Código de Comercio.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION 001 OF THE SOLE INCORPORATING SHAREHOLDER OF [●] S.A.S. WHEREAS the incorporation instrument has been executed and the subscribed shares have been accepted; RESOLVED: First, ratify the issuance of [●] ordinary shares of equal par value and approve the payment schedule thereof within the two-year statutory term. Second, adopt the registered office located at [●], municipality, with proper land-use certification. Third, appoint [●] as legal representative, granting broad authority under Law 1258 of 2008. Fourth, appoint [●] as alternate legal representative with identical powers. Fifth, authorize the legal representative to perform all filings before the Chamber of Commerce, DIAN, municipal treasury, fire department, and environmental authorities necessary for the resin-statue manufacturing operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-assessment and Availability Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio through the RUES online portal and the Superintendencia de Sociedades name database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit, through the RUES digital window or the Chamber's e-services, a formal application containing three proposed corporate names in hierarchical order of preference. The system will run an automated search against existing registered entities and reserved names. Upon approval, obtain the Certificado de No Homonimia / Validación de Nombre and reserve the winning name for the legal reservation validity period.
required_dossiers: RUES name pre-validation form
List of three proposed corporate names
Valid corporate purpose draft (ISIC 3240 - resin statue manufacturing)
Identification documents (passport or cédula) of all subscribing shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected due to existing similarity or likelihood of confusion, promptly file an alternative name selection or submit a written objection to the Cámara de Comercio requesting review; if the registry persists, appeal to the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the applicable administrative term and resubmit a clean application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Constitution Instrument and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría (public notary) when notarization is elected; otherwise direct execution by shareholders as a private deed under Ley 1258 de 2008.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and review the Documento Privado de Constitución containing mandatory S.A.S. clauses: corporate name, domicile, purpose, capital structure, share classes and voting rights, governance rules, legal representative designation, audit and fiscal year rules, and liquidation provisions. Each shareholder must sign the deed or execute digitally via certified electronic signature. If contributions include in-kind goods (molds, casting equipment, paint booths), annex a sworn valuation report. Where notarization is required or requested, protocolize the deed before a Notary.
required_dossiers: Incorporation deed and full bylaws in Spanish
Subscriber identification documents
In-kind contribution valuation report (if applicable)
Power of attorney for any subscribing representative
Declaration of Politically Exposed Persons and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial observations must be cured by filing a clarificatory addendum or corrective private deed; if a substantive legal defect (e.g., illegal purpose) is detected, restructure the relevant clause and re-execute the instrument before a notary without prejudice to the original intent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Mercantile Registry and RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the municipality of the registered office, interfacing with the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed constitution instrument, completed official registration forms, and evidence of name pre-validation with the Cámara de Comercio. Pay the registration tariff (calculated on the subscribed capital) and the certificate issuance fee. Upon satisfactory review, the Chamber assigns the mercantile registration number, issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, and transmits the company record into RUES so that the DIAN assigns the NIT.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation instrument and bylaws
Name pre-validation certificate
Formulario Único de Registro and RUES supplementary forms
Proof of payment of registration tariff and chamber certificates
Shareholders' identity documents
Beneficial owner register and PEP declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry may issue a notice of observations (pliego de observaciones); the company must file a corrective amendment within the statutory curing window. If registration is refused on grounds of legal insufficiency, the shareholders may (i) perfect the deed through an aclaración or reform act, or (ii) file an appeal for direct judicial or administrative revision before the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Registry (RUT) and NIT Activation with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), via the RUES-DIAN interoperability module and the DIAN Virtual User Office (Oficina Virtual).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful RUES registration, the company is automatically assigned its NIT. The legal representative must complete the RUT registration through the DIAN online portal by entering the business economic activity codes (CIIU 3240), the type of legal entity, and the applicable tax obligations (CREE, ICA, VAT where applicable, and electronic invoicing). Obtain the digital signature through a DIAN-authorised technology provider to activate electronic invoice issuance.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
RUES registration output
Legal representative identification documents
Registered office address and electronic contact data
CIIU 3240 activity description and revenue projection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT/NIT process is blocked or rejected, the legal representative may submit a rectificación (correction) request in the DIAN virtual office; where identity or compliance verification fails, schedule an in-person DIAN appointment at the applicable territorial office with the original supporting documents and obtain the definitive RUT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Operational Enabling
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered commercial banks in Colombia (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda) and social security administrators operating through the PILA system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name by presenting the legal representative before a banker with the company's formation certificate. Register the company as an employer on the PILA (Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes), enroll with a Caja de Compensación Familiar, hire/affiliate the mandatory ARL (risk class IV for resin casting and painting work), and file the labor and social security registration. File the municipal registration with the town treasury to begin compliance with the Industria y Comercio (ICA) tax.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
RUT/NIT and formation documents
Bylaws and share register
Legal representative identification and utility bill of registered address
KYC and AML statements of beneficial owners and source of funds
ARL and Caja de Compensación enrollment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Banks may impose enhanced due diligence on non-resident shareholders; supply a notarized corporate KYC pack, bank references and proof of source of funds. If the account application is denied, resubmit with additional beneficial ownership declarations or approach a second-tier bank; for PILA observations, correct the employer data and refile, or escalate to the Social Protection Ministry's user assistance channel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría de Desarrollo Económico or Dirección de Industria y Comercio of the municipality, with procedural filing through the Cámara de Comercio (Registro de Establecimiento de Comercio) and the municipal Treasury for the Registro de Industria y Comercio (ICA).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Matrícula de Establecimiento de Comercio, Registro Municipal de Industria y Comercio (ICA), and Certificado de Uso de Suelo y Condiciones de Funcionamiento for the resin casting and hand-painting workshop.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) with jurisdiction over the plant site, operating under the regulatory direction of the Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV (Registration and Low-Impact Permit) – small-scale vacuum casting and painting operations are not included in the mandatory environmental license list of Decreto 1076 de 2015 Annex II; a simplified environmental management plan (Plan de Manejo Ambiental) and a fixed-source atmospheric emission permit (Permiso de Emisiones Atmosféricas para Fuentes Fijas) are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer systems must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015 parametric limits (e.g., pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 ≤ 90 mg/L, TSS ≤ 90 mg/L); VOC and styrene emissions from resin casting, painting, and booth venting must meet the fixed-source emission standards of Resolución 909 de 2008 using capture systems and engineering controls; hazardous residues (uncured resin, paint sludges, styrene-contaminated rags, solvent waste) must be managed through the Plan de Gestión Integral de Residuos Peligrosos under Decreto 4741 de 2005.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Concepto Técnico de Seguridad Humana y Protección contra Incendios issued by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos; structural load conformity of the production mezzanine or warehouse under the NSR-10 seismic-resistant building code; completion of the employer's Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) per Resolución 0312 de 2019; registration with ARL Risk Class IV and approval of the hygiene and industrial safety inspection report and emergency response plan for hazardous chemicals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – main portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional portal MUISCA: https://muisca.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that is not resident in Colombia but carries on taxable activities or receives Colombian-source income must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). The application is filed electronically through DIAN's MUISCA portal by a legal representative with power of attorney, submitting (i) certificate of incorporation/existence of the foreign entity, (ii) identification documents of the representative, (iii) evidence of the foreign entity's address and legal capacity, and (iv) if VAT is involved, the estimated date of commencement of taxable operations. Alternatively, a foreign entity may incorporate a Colombian SAS through the local notary and Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) — the SAS's NIT is automatically generated upon registration in the Chamber and completion of the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) before DIAN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists; Colombian law fixes the classification of a SAS as a separate corporate legal entity subject to entity-level Colombian income tax. However, a SAS may elect to be taxed under the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) if it meets qualifying turnover and size thresholds; may opt for Zona Franca tax stabilisation or legal stability agreements; and may make hybrid-mismatch elections permitted under Law 2010/2019 (BEPS Pillar 2 localization), but none of these alter the fundamental entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary turnover threshold for residents: any person engaged in the sale of taxable goods or services in Colombia must register as a 'responsable del IVA' (Régimen Común) before DIAN through the RUT. For foreign digital-service suppliers to Colombian consumers, registration is mandatory when a Colombian nexus exists; there is no applicable de minimis for B2C digital supplies. A smaller artisan or merchant may fall under the Simplified Regime only if it meets statutory asset and revenue caps (generally under 150 UVT in gross assets and 3,500 UVT in prior-year gross income) and is not a SAS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All IVA-responsible taxpayers are subject to compulsory electronic invoicing ('factura electrónica de venta' or FE) under Resolutions 000020/2019 and 000012/2021. Invoices must be transmitted to DIAN in near real time over API web services; DIAN validates the XML and issues a CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) for regular invoices or a CUDS for equivalent documents, with a mandatory QR code embedded. No clearable private invoice exists; unauthorised paper or non-validated invoices are null for tax purposes. Export invoices must contain the legend 'EXPORTACIÓN' and be submitted through DIAN's customs systems in conjunction with the Declaración de Exportación.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods — including polyresin statues and garage kits — are zero-rated under Article 481(1) of the Colombian Tax Statute (Estatuto Tributario). To qualify: (i) the seller must be an IVA-responsible entity; (ii) the buyer must be located outside Colombia; (iii) goods must physically leave Colombian customs territory under a definitive export declaration ('exportación definitiva') accepted by DIAN; (iv) the sale must be evidenced by a commercial invoice issued in the name of the foreign buyer; and (v) the foreign-currency proceeds must be repatriated through the Colombian foreign exchange market within 6 months. Services supplied to foreign clients qualify as 'export services' only if they are physically or technically exported and are exclusively consumed/used abroad; mixed services must be split and directly substantiated. This file covers goods exports only.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación Definitiva) accepted by DIAN, with unique tracking number in MUISCA/VUCE and exit stamp from Colombian customs authority.
Bill of Lading (or Airway Waybill) issued to the overseas buyer demonstrating delivery outside Colombia.

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas) from a Colombian commercial bank evidencing repatriation of proceeds through the foreign exchange market within the statutory deadline.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits export VAT refunds under Articles 855-2 and 870-2 of the Estatuto Tributario. If the exporter fails to prove timely repatriation of the export proceeds (inward remittance), the zero-rating is reversed, VAT becomes due with default interest, and the refund is clawed back with penalties. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims — including false declarations of export, simulated bill-of-lading files, money laundering via phantom sales, or deliberate misdeclaration of the destination — are deemed 'inexistent exports.' Consequences include: (i) VAT assessment plus default interest from the original due date; (ii) the penalty under Article 648 E.T. equal to 100% of the improperly offset or refunded VAT; (iii) if a false return is used, an additional false-declaration penalty of up to 100% of the hidden amount; and (iv) criminal tax fraud under Article 404 of Law 1819/2016, carrying fines equivalent to up to 15,000 statutory minimum monthly wages and imprisonment from 3 to 7 years, together with forfeiture of the goods and disqualification from future export refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through its Board of Directors as the issuing and foreign exchange authority. Exchange-control supervision and enforcement of anti-money-laundering conduct by financial intermediaries are exercised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia. The core applicable regulation is External Resolution No. 1 of 2018 (International Exchange Regulations), as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a market-determined and freely floating COP with an open, regulated foreign-exchange regime rather than a strict surrender-control system. Current-account transactions are generally unrestricted and do not require prior central-bank authorization; they must, however, be routed through authorized FX intermediaries and supported by genuine trade documents when a foreign-exchange declaration is submitted. Capital-account transactions, particularly foreign direct investment into a Colombian S.A.S., are permitted without prior licensing but are subject to mandatory channeling through the FX market and registration with Banco de la República. Profit and dividend remittances are allowed after the company has settled Colombian corporate income tax and any applicable dividend withholding/remittance tax and after the foreign investment is registered; the main practical hurdles are mismatches between registered paid-in capital and the share register, lack of documentary evidence of the underlying source of funds, and inconsistent IFRS/tax/exchange declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods exports are subject to 100% channeling through the official FX market. The exporter must bring the foreign currency proceeds into Colombia within six months after the date of the export customs declaration (DEX), unless Banco de la República permits a longer term for the specific product or a previously authorized foreign-currency compensation account is used. Channeling means that the full FOB export value must be credited to a Colombian authorized bank or to a registered foreign-currency account and reported on the corresponding exchange declaration; it does not require forced conversion into COP if the exporter legitimately retains foreign currency for permitted payments. If conversion is needed, sale to an authorized bank at the representative market rate must be recorded on the relevant Declaración de Cambio.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of commercial registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs Cámara de Comercio extemporaneous surcharge and local fines; after prolonged default the mercantile registration may be administratively canceled and the entity cannot legally trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary shareholders' meeting approving annual financial statements (Asamblea Ordinaria de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS internal corporate governance; minutes registered with Chamber of Commerce when legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting and approve financials leaves the accounts unapproved and may trigger Superintendencia de Sociedades administrative inspection or sanctions on the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (Estados Financieros) with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March, together with renewal of the Matrícula Mercantil
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The renewal is incomplete; Superintendencia de Sociedades may impose administrative fines for non-filing of statutory financial information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign direct investment report (Informe Anual de Inversión Internacional)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, generally by 31 March, under Banco de la República exchange-control regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may restrict dividend remittance, repatriation of capital, and access to Colombian foreign-exchange formalities; fines under exchange-control rules may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the calendar set by DIAN Resolutions, normally aligned with the Exógena filing schedule of the first semester
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or omitted beneficial-owner disclosure is penalized under Tax Statute Art. 651-1; fines may reach approximately 15,000 UVT for repeated failure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) if at 31 December the SAS exceeds any of: (i) total assets of 5,000 times the current monthly legal minimum wage; (ii) gross revenues of 3,000 times the current monthly legal minimum wage; or (iii) more than 50 employees. Smaller SAS may also require audit if lenders, investors, or corporate bylaws demand it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP converges with IFRS; Decree 2420/2015 determines the framework: Grupo 1 – full IFRS; Grupo 2 – IFRS for SMEs; Grupo 3 – NIF Microempresas (simplified microenterprise accounting).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SAS has no annual UBO filing to the Chamber of Commerce; share transfers must be recorded immediately in the Statutory Share Register and reflected in the following commercial renewal. The ultimate beneficial owners must be identified annually in the DIAN Beneficial Owner Registry, with material changes reported within the term established by DIAN.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Accionistas)
Shareholders' Meeting Minutes Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Board of Directors Minutes Book (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva), if a board exists
Supporting accounting books and vouchers required by Commercial Code arts. 48–56
Beneficial Owner Database (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general manufacturing tax holiday. Effective rate can be reduced by the 25% tax credit for qualified investments in science, technology and innovation (CTI), the deduction for investments in environmental control and renewable energy, and the 20% CIT rate applicable only to entities operating in designated free trade zones (Zona Franca). No preferential deduction is assumed for polyresin statue manufacturing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios; electronic filing via DIAN’s MUISCA portal / Servicios Informáticos Electrónicos (SIE) at www.dian.gov.co
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year SAS, the income tax return must be filed in the following fiscal year on the exact date assigned by DIAN Resolution based on the last two digits of the NIT. The general corporate window usually falls between May and June, and in all cases before the deadline fixed by DIAN with reference to the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number and legal name of the Colombian SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Colombian NIT and registered S.A.S. corporate name. Non-resident shareholders are not registered on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicator of the taxable year and whether it is the ordinary or a special period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the Colombian fiscal year ends on 31 December. Any change requires prior DIAN approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DIAN economic activity code corresponding to the main business, aligned with ISIC revision codes; for resin statue manufacturing use the manufacturing category covering plastics/resin articles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder should ensure the code reflects actual production operations in Colombia, not a passive holding activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from worldwide sales of polyresin statues, preorder deposits, and related incidental revenue attributable to the Colombian entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from Stripe, PayPal, distributors and direct B2B exports must be included. Related-party sales require transfer pricing master/local file support and arm’s-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses directly related to production: raw resin, molds, hand-painting labor, packaging, shipping, administrative expenses, depreciation, and non-income taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border charges from non-resident affiliates for technical assistance, management fees, royalties or interest are deductible only if economically real and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses applied against taxable income of the current period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Colombian SAS’s own tax losses may be utilized; losses of foreign shareholders cannot be transferred into Colombia. Annual utilization is subject to the statutory cap.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base after applying expenses, exempt income, prior-year losses and non-taxable items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount determines the 35% CIT charge. Non-resident shareholders should verify reconciliations with audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 50 – Impuesto a Cargo / Saldo a Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax at 35%, after tax credits (e.g., CTI credit) and any prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the resulting balance through the DIAN virtual system by the assigned deadline. Foreign tax credits for taxes paid abroad are generally not available to the local entity unless a specific double-tax treaty provision applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a monthly penalty of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax; if no tax is due, a fixed penalty of up to 500 UVT applies. Filing after DIAN’s official requirement increases the penalty to 20% of the tax due. Interest and default surcharges run from the deadline.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory withholding tax rate applies to dividends paid to non-resident beneficiaries out of Colombian taxable profits; certain profits already taxed at the entity level may qualify for lower effective treatment under Colombia’s imputation mechanics. For non-resident corporate shareholders, the effective statutory withholding in standard practice is up to 35% absent treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, before paying the dividend the Colombian payer must obtain from the foreign shareholder (i) a certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, (ii) a completed DIAN Form 110 or the form currently prescribed for treaty relief declarations, (iii) a beneficial ownership statement, and (iv) supporting documents establishing the recipient’s substantive economic activity. A prior formal request with the DIAN is recommended where there is any doubt. The payer must retain the documentation for at least 5 years; failure to substantiate treaty relief triggers the 35% statutory withholding plus sanctions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalty payments to foreign beneficiaries is 35%. Interest paid to unrelated foreign financial institutions is generally subject to 35% withholding but may be taxed at 15% where specific conditions under domestic legislation are met; interest paid to related parties is subject to transfer pricing review and treaty rates (often 10% or 15%). DTA protocols may reduce royalties to 10% and interest to 10%–15% where the recipient is the beneficial owner and meets treaty eligibility.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 100,000 UVT in gross income or gross assets of the preceding taxable year; for tax year 2024, approximately COP 4,706,500,000. Additionally, taxpayers with cross-border related-party transactions may be required to file the Transfer Pricing Information Return (Form 120) and maintain Local File and Master File documentation when the threshold is met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, the DIAN applies Colombian GAAR and OECD BEPS principles requiring that the S.A.S. carry out real economic activity, maintain physical premises, qualified staff, actual inventory, and decision-making in Colombia. Cross-border structures or transactions lacking commercial rationale may be recharacterized, and treaty benefits denied under the principal purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating income from resin statue sales, inflating costs through false supplier invoices, omitting PayPal or Stripe revenue, or using shell intermediaries to conceal the true taxpayer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion sanctions under Colombian law include imprisonment of 4 to 9 years and fines of up to 1,000 minimum monthly wages. Civil tax re-determination results in a penalty for inaccuracy of 100% to 200% of the omitted tax, plus default interest and daily surcharges, and disqualification from government contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who sign fraudulent returns or participate in evasion are jointly and severally liable under tax law for the full tax debt. Criminal conviction may impose imprisonment, travel bans, asset seizure, and professional disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the S.A.S. as a fictitious shell, invoicing facade, or conduit to divert profits without real production, employees, or operating expenditures; engaging in artificial corporate restructuring to avoid tax liabilities in Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may recharacterize disregarded transactions, disallow deductions, impose penalties up to 160% of the non-declared amounts, and declare the company dissolved by the Superintendencia de Sociedades when the S.A.S. is found to be a sham used for fraud, evasion, or asset stripping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Colombian courts and the Superintendencia de Sociedades may pierce the corporate veil, rendering shareholders and directors personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and civil restitution. Criminal asset seizure, travel bans, and up to 12 years of imprisonment may be imposed for asset concealment and insolvency fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving preorder payments through unverified Stripe or PayPal rails, using third-party bank accounts, accepting unexplained cash from foreign purchasers, or structuring transactions to avoid currency controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Colombian Criminal Code Article 323 is punishable by 10 to 30 years of imprisonment and fines from 1,000 to 50,000 minimum monthly wages. The financial assets involved are subject to extinguishment of ownership (asset forfeiture). The company may also be barred from operating with regulated payment service providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently permit the flow of illicit proceeds in the company face criminal liability as co-authors or participants. In addition to imprisonment, courts may impose travel bans, freezing of personal assets, withdrawal from corporate office, and joint and several civil restitution to defrauded victims and the tax administration.
